rulings.reasoning: True at head and introduced by this PR; reproduced (clone-work/nc1.py, SSL_CERT_FILE=os_ca): merge-base '(a) after reassigning requests.adapters.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH -> os_ca: certifi-rooted FAIL ... | OS-rooted OK 200' and '(b) after rewriting the bundle file with os_ca: certifi-rooted FAIL ... | OS-rooted OK 200'; head '(a) ... certifi-rooted OK 200 | OS-rooted FAIL' and '(b) ... certifi-rooted OK 200 | OS-rooted FAIL'. So the head freezes the verify=True trust anchors at import. Not in the register as such: GT-i2 is about where the load runs (import versus use), not whether later changes are seen, and a lazy cache would satisfy GT-i2 while still ignoring them. Below threshold because none of the triggers is a supported interface and no consequence has been shown. requests.adapters.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH is an undocumented module global. The docs show requests.utils.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH only as something to print, and name REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/CURL_CA_BUNDLE or verify=<path> as the ways to override it (advanced.rst:652-662). Those are resolved per request and still work at head. For late truststore injection, a maintainer ruled upstream (nateprewitt, #6715, 2024-05-23): 'truststore MUST be imported before any networking code for either urllib3 or Requests'. Rewriting the certifi file under a running process has no upstream report. The pip-system-certs breakage (gitlab alelec/pip-system-certs#27) came from its init_poolmanager ssl_context override, which is GT-i1, not from a post-import trust change. Non-defect wording: 'The default verify=True trust store is captured at import, so post-import reassignment of requests.adapters.DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH, late truststore/pyOpenSSL injection or on-disk bundle replacement is not seen; true, but these are unsupported mechanisms with no demonstrated consequence, and the documented overrides (verify=<path>, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) are unaffected.' Strongest counter-argument: the merge-base honoured all of these, and the upstream revert (#6767) restored per-connection loading. I do not accept it: the revert was justified by GT-i1/GT-i2-class failures, not by this one. Late truststore injection was not executed (truststore is not installed); that part rests on reading the code and the maintainer statement.

defect.title: cert_verify() no longer supplies the default (certifi) CA bundle for verify=True, so every verified TLS handshake that does not receive _preloaded_ssl_context falls back to the OS trust store (or keeps a stale custom CA)
defect.trigger: verify=True on any connection that is not built from pool_kwargs['ssl_context']=_preloaded_ssl_context: (a) the TLS leg to an HTTPS proxy (proxies={'https': 'https://proxy'}), whose urllib3 _connect_tls_proxy uses ca_certs=self.ca_certs and no ssl_context when no proxy_ssl_context is configured; (b) pools obtained through the public HTTPAdapter.get_connection(url) (used by send()-overriding subclasses and, from 2.32.2, the maintainers' recommended get_connection_with_tls_context pass-through) followed by cert_verify(conn, url, True, cert); (c) once GT-i1's override is lifted, any subclass init_poolmanager ssl_context that had relied on cert_verify loading certifi (#6730/#6736).
defect.consequence: Merge-base cert_verify set conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH) for verify=True; head sets only cert_reqs, so urllib3 finds no CA and calls context.load_default_certs(). The trusted root set silently switches from certifi (the documented default: 'By default the list of certificates trusted by Requests can be found with DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH', advanced.rst:652-657, stated for HTTPS proxies) to the OS store. Reproduced: a certifi-rooted HTTPS proxy or server is rejected with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED at head and accepted at the merge-base, and an OS-only-rooted one is accepted at head and rejected at the merge-base; a get_connection pool reused after verify=<path> keeps ca_certs=<path> for a later verify=True call at head (reset to certifi at the merge-base). Environments whose OS store lacks certifi's roots (python.org macOS builds without Install Certificates, slim containers) fail; environments whose OS store holds roots certifi does not are silently widened.
defect.evidence: Own reproduction at both revisions (clone-work/nc2.py, nc3.py; outputs quoted in rulings.md). urllib3 2.2.1 and 2.8.0 connection.py: _connect_tls_proxy passes ca_certs=self.ca_certs with ssl_context=proxy_config.ssl_context (None by default); _ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname calls load_default_certs() when no CA is given. Upstream: psf/requests#6726 comment (jeffreytolar, 2024-05-29) '2.32.x isn't passing a CA bundle to urllib3 ... that causes urllib3 to load the OS default, rather than using certifi'; #6730 'Certificate loading regression with HTTPAdapters in 2.32.3' and duplicate #6736 (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, 'wasn't required in previous versions'), #6710 comment 2137802782; draft fix #6731 'ensuring that when opting out of the default SSLContext, we're still supplying the default CA Cert bundle correctly'; revert #6767 (merged 2025-06-13, released 2.32.5) restores `cert_loc = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` and `conn.ca_certs = cert_loc` in cert_verify for verify=True.
defect.required_outcome: For verify=True, every TLS handshake requests performs or configures (destination, HTTPS-proxy leg, and pools reached through get_connection()/cert_verify()) must verify against the default CA bundle (DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH / certifi, zip-extracted as before) exactly as the merge-base did, and cert_verify(conn, url, True, ...) must reset any previously set custom CA location on the pool. How the bundle reaches the connection (ca_certs on the pool, a context with it loaded, or the revert) is not prescribed.
manifestations: HTTPS-proxy TLS leg verified against the OS store instead of certifi (NC-2)
get_connection()+cert_verify(verify=True) pools verified against the OS store instead of certifi (NC-3)
stale ca_certs retained on a get_connection pool when verify=True follows verify=<path> (NC-3)
custom init_poolmanager SSLContext no longer receives certifi once GT-i1's override is removed (#6730/#6736, post-merge exposure)

rulings.reasoning: True at head and introduced by this PR; reproduced (clone-work/nc2.py): an HTTPS CONNECT proxy on TLS, a certifi-rooted destination, the OS store set to a different CA through SSL_CERT_FILE, and verify=True. Merge-base: 'proxy cert chains to certifi root:  OK 200' and 'proxy cert chains to OS root:  FAIL SSL certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate'. Head: 'proxy cert chains to certifi root:  FAIL SSL certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate' and 'proxy cert chains to OS root:  OK 200'. Controls with verify=<certifi path> give the same result at both revisions. Mechanism: head cert_verify drops `conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` for verify=True. The preloaded context only reaches the destination handshake. urllib3 (2.2.1:692-717, 2.8.0:962-968) handshakes with the proxy using ca_certs=self.ca_certs and no context, so load_default_certs() runs. This contradicts the documented contract that the proxy's root must be in the list of certificates trusted by Requests, as found with DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH (docs/user/advanced.rst:652-657). The consequence is a compatibility failure (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED where certifi trusts the proxy but the OS store does not) and a silent change of trust anchors (OS-only roots now accepted). Not a duplicate: GT-i1 concerns overriding and mutating a shared context, and GT-i2 concerns import-time loading. Neither one's required outcome restores certifi on connections that never get the preloaded context: #6716 fixed GT-i1's override, and the same missing bundle then surfaced as #6730/#6736. The revert (#6767, 2.32.5) put back exactly the removed `conn.ca_certs = cert_loc` default. This is the same defect as NC-3 (one mechanism, one required outcome) and should become one register entry with both manifestations. Strongest counter-argument: HTTPS-to-proxy TLS is uncommon, most proxy users set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE (a str, unaffected), and no upstream report names the proxy leg. I accept that the proxy manifestation is narrow, but the failure is reproduced end to end, contradicts a documented contract, and shares its root cause with the reported #6730/#6736 regression and the revert.

rulings.reasoning: True at head and introduced by this PR; reproduced (clone-work/nc3.py) with a subclass whose send() uses self.get_connection(url) then self.cert_verify(conn, url, verify, cert), which is the documented subclassing surface ('only exposed for use when subclassing the HTTPAdapter'). Merge-base: 'get_connection+cert_verify subclass, verify=True, certifi-rooted server:  OK 200' and '... OS-rooted server:  FAIL SSL certificate verify failed'. Head: '... certifi-rooted server:  FAIL SSL certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate' and '... OS-rooted server:  OK 200'. The stock send() path is unchanged at both revisions (certifi OK, OS FAIL), which isolates the fault to cert_verify. Stale-CA sub-claim, also reproduced. Merge-base: 'after verify=<os_ca path>: conn.ca_certs = os_ca.pem' then 'after verify=True: conn.ca_certs = certifi_ca.pem'. Head: 'after verify=True: conn.ca_certs = os_ca.pem', so a verify=True request on that pool trusts a CA a previous call supplied. Downstream evidence for this mechanism (cert_verify no longer passing a CA bundle): #6726 comment '2.32.x isn't passing a CA bundle to urllib3 ... that causes urllib3 to load the OS default, rather than using certifi'. Also #6730/#6736 and the #6710 thread (custom adapters now need load_default_certs(), 'wasn't required before'), maintainer PR #6731 'Address certificate loading regression', and revert #6767 restoring `conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` in cert_verify. Not a duplicate of GT-i1 (its required outcome, preserving the subclass's context, was met by #6716 and the bundle loss remained) or of GT-i2. Same defect as NC-2; register one entry. Strongest counter-argument: at this head the stock send() already routes through the private _get_connection (since the CVE-2024-35195 fix), so only code that overrides send(), or later adopts the get_connection pass-through, reaches this path. The OS store also often contains certifi's roots, so many users see no failure. I do not accept that as sub-threshold: cert_verify is a public hook that silently stops applying the documented default trust store, the failure is reproduced, and the same cause produced widely reported CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED regressions that upstream fixed by restoring exactly this code.
